statement_en: That there is a quantitative sleep law for a teleost: sleep time predicted from body or brain mass, as Savage and West 2007 do for mammals.
reason_detail: The only quantitative sleep theory fetched is for mammals (96 species) and predicts sleep time from brain mass. No source gives a quantitative sleep law for a teleost, and none was found for day/night activity either. Rather than extrapolate the mammalian relation across a class boundary, or fit a constant to the two zebrafish sleep measurements that exist, the thread declared NO LAW and left the Studio's sleep perturbation with no Lean row.
what_was_tried: Fetching a quantitative sleep theory: Savage and West 2007 (PMID 17215372), mammals only, 96 species, brain-mass predictor.
Searching for a teleost equivalent and for a day/night activity law: none found.

The alternative -- fitting a constant to the available zebrafish sleep numbers -- was available and was NOT taken, because those numbers are themselves definition-dependent (see open question oq-larval-sleep-definition: 58.2% vs 83.9% for the same stage).
what_survives: The refusal is the result. lean/Delphi/Perturb.lean carries the gap explicitly -- "Sleep: NO LAW ... Nothing is invented: the Studio's sleep and day/night perturbations have no Lean row" -- and the same section records that grip and predator escape likewise have no law. A Studio perturbation with no row is honest; a row fitted to a definition-dependent number would have been a law that looked checkable and was not. The measurements themselves survive as recorded observations in sim-engine/scenarios/sleep.mjs, side by side and never mixed.

lean_ref.note: deliberately NO declaration; the module docstring section 6 records the absence and the reason

evidence.claim: The declared absence of a law, with the reason, in the Lean module itself.
evidence.quote: **Sleep: NO LAW.** The only quantitative theory fetched (Savage and West 2007, PMID 17215372) is for mammals (96 species) and predicts sleep time from brain mass; no source gives a quantitative sleep law for a teleost, and none was found for day/night activity. Nothing is invented: the Studio's sleep and day/night perturbations have no Lean row. Grip and predator escape likewise have no law here.
evidence.kind: declared gap with its reason, in the module that would have carried the law

found_by: Harvested from lean/Delphi/Perturb.lean, which declares the absence rather than leaving it implicit.

history.change: harvested by the open-questions thread from the thread that published the failure

added proof_status and attempted:false. The new never-attempted invariant caught this record: its reason (abandoned-for-lack-of-a-constant) means nothing was ever tried in Lean, and without proof_status a reader could have taken it for a statement that was attempted and failed. Also set do_not_repropose false: an untried statement must stay available to propose if a teleost sleep law is ever published.

proof_status: NO LEAN DECLARATION WAS EVER WRITTEN, and Lean never checked anything here. This is not a statement that was attempted and defeated: no quantitative teleost sleep law existed to formalise, so lean/Delphi/Perturb.lean records the absence deliberately ("Sleep: NO LAW") rather than carrying a declaration. Nothing about a teleost sleep law has been established or refuted.
